(a) **Decreasing order of stability of compounds:** Stability in organic intermediates or systems generally follows resonance > hyperconjugation > inductive effects. (For alkenes, stability increases with the degree of alkyl substitution due to hyperconjugation: Tri-substituted > Di-substituted > Mono-substituted).

(b) **Short Notes:**
- **(i) Electromeric effect ($E$-effect):** It is a temporary polarization effect occurring in multi-bonded (unsaturated) organic compounds in the presence of an attacking reagent. The $\pi$-electrons are completely transferred to one of the atoms. It is denoted as $+E$ (when displacement is away from the attacking reagent) or $-E$ (when displacement is towards the attacking reagent).
- **(ii) Allnes:** Also known as cumulenes with adjacent double bonds ($>C=C=C<$). They exhibit axial chirality (stereoisomerism without a chiral center) when terminal carbons carry different substituents, resulting in enantiomerism.

(c) **Atropisomerism:** A subtype of conformational stereoisomerism where isomers arise from restricted rotation about a single bond, where the steric hindrance barrier to rotation is high enough to allow isolation of the individual conformers (e.g., substituted biphenyls).

(d) **Singlet vs Triplet Carbene:**
| Feature | Singlet Carbene | Triplet Carbene |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Spin State** | Electron spins are paired ($S = 0$) | Electron spins are parallel ($S = 1$) |
| **Orbital State** | $sp^2$ hybridized, lone pair in $sp^2$, empty $p$-orbital | $sp$ hybridized, two unbonded electrons in orthogonal $p$-orbitals |
| **Geometry** | Bent | Linear or bent |

(e) **Favorski Rearrangement:**
-$\alpha$-Haloketones react with bases to yield rearranged carboxylic acids, esters, or amides via a cyclopropanone intermediate.
- **Mechanism:** Base abstracts an acidic proton to form an enolate, which undergoes intramolecular nucleophilic substitution (displacement of halide) to form a highly strained cyclopropanone intermediate. Nucleophilic attack by $\text{OH}^-$ ring-opens the intermediate to yield the more stable rearranged carboxylate product.
